review: Request: at round 14 Lin (energy 38.8, standing about 1.1 m from the mature berry plant commons-berry-0-0, owning only the berry stack item-6-lin-57) asked for a practical way to tend or propagate an existing berry plant for a dependable local food supply, with learning that takes world time and physical effects that need real work and suitable conditions. World Agent decision: develop (learning 3) a general water_plant(target, waterItem, carrier, quantityLitres) operation with real collection and carrying of water, a conserved soil-water input bound to the existing soil moisture and growth code, refusal when measured conditions do not justify watering, no growth claim and no reward. Narrowed scope decided by the user: the water source is a small amount of visible river or shallow water within hand reach, taken by hand or with a water vessel that already exists (no vessel making and no new container); real energy costs to collect and to pour; spillage of hand-held water while carrying and in the pour; the target is only the soil plot of an existing rooted plant object (no bare ground or general terrain watering); the effect exists only where the package is installed; and the study cost, refusal before any cost when the measured moisture already meets the plant requirement or the soil is waterlogged, no growth claim and no reward are kept. Implemented (full mechanism): rooted-plant-watering@1 (ability rooted-plant-watering, handler long.rooted-plant-watering, equivalence plant:root-zone-water-dose:1, learning 3 with no study energy, 2,279 code units, appended last to the package list) with modes collect, water and status, each one round. collect (x, y of a personally visible ~ or = cell whose edge is within 0.65 m of a person standing on the bank with a clear reach, reusing waterSurface of the ex10 river-contact-water@1 helpers) costs 0.3 energy and fills two cupped hands to 0.2 L, or an owned item with an existing water vessel record to its capacity; a represented finite river compartment, if one exists, is debited, otherwise the withdrawal is recorded per source in the person's hand record. Hand water is a per-person state record, not an inventory item: at each round end, the collection round included, 40% of what is left leaks and 20% more per metre walked (compounded), and below 0.005 L it is gone; it is lost at death. water (target: a growing plant object rooted in the ground and within reach; quantityLitres optional, default all held, at most 0.5 L) costs 2 energy per litre poured (at least 0.05); 20% of a hand pour (5% from a vessel) misses the root zone and the rest is delivered to the root zone of the plant's 1 m x 1 m terrain cell, shared by every plant rooted in it, where water above saturation runs off. It is refused before any cost, with the measured values, when soil moisture already meets the plant requirement (for Lin's berry plant 0.65 against 0.6, so its growth water factor is already 1), when the plot is waterlogged (hazard waterlogging above 0.1 or moisture at least 1.3), when the target is not a rooted growing plant (reeds, items, water cells, bare ground), when it is out of reach, or when no water is held. status (no energy) reports the held water, the plot moisture, requirement, waterlogging and the root-zone record. A new module stores retained root-zone litres per watered cell with documented parameters: 30 L raise the 0-1.5 moisture index of the top 0.15 m of one square metre by 1, field capacity at index 1 (half the water above it drains below the root zone each round), saturation at 1.3 (the excess runs off), and evaporation of 10% of the retained water per round, at most 0.0375 L (3 L per square metre per 80-round day), with a last trace below 1 mL evaporating; each cell keeps a closed ledger (received = retained + runoff + drained + evaporated) and each hand record another (collected = held + poured + carry spill, poured = delivered + pour spill), both asserted. One gated hook in openConditions adds the retained water to the ground-derived moisture only when a cell record with retained litres exists and rooted-plant-watering@1 is installed, so the existing plant update (openPlants and forestGrowth, unchanged) reads it through its own min(1, moisture / requirement) rule and waterlogging penalty; without that revision or without delivered water openConditions returns exactly what it returned before (tested, including a stray record in a world without the revision, which replays identically). Events plant-watering-collected, -poured, -spilled, -plot-dry and -status carry view metadata (operation, actor, phase, target, cell, carrier, litres, progress) with visualComponents empty; the practice evidence is plant-watering-poured, which never carries a qualified flag, so there is no practice milestone, satisfaction source or reward. Assumptions: (1) the root zone is the terrain cell under the plant, so a dose is shared by all plants rooted in that cell and also raises the soil moisture read anywhere in that cell; (2) the cell's ground-derived moisture for retention, runoff and drainage is measured at the cell centre; (3) the added water is the first to evaporate and to drain, and the ground-derived base is left unchanged; (4) hands leak by the stated fractions whatever else the person does, and other actions do not empty them at once; (5) the ex23 river is not represented as finite, so a hand scoop does not deplete it; (6) a vessel's own leakage belongs to its own package and is not modelled here; (7) watering a plot whose moisture is already above the requirement is refused rather than allowed as a no-op. A throwaway check on the archived round-14 world installed the package, had Lin learn it in three rounds and refused water on commons-berry-0-0 before any cost with soil moisture 0.65, waterlogging 0 and requirement 0.6; it was deleted afterwards. What Lin can do now: after three study rounds, scoop water by hand at a river bank, carry it with real leakage and pour it on a rooted plant whose measured soil is drier than it needs, and read the plot with status; one hand scoop carried 0.8 m in one round delivers about 0.048 L, which raises the cell's moisture by about 0.0016 and evaporates within about 40 rounds. Her own berry plant is correctly refused because it is not water-limited, and in this world every plant whose measured soil is below its requirement (now the plum on rocky ground, fern-root and fungus plots; during the drought also the western berry, root, hazelnut and acorn plants) stands at least 12.7 m from river or shallow water, so no hand-carried water survives the walk: today the operation can be used only on such plots within a few metres of water, for example newly established plants there or plots in a drought that reaches the river. First release: no; the narrowed scope is implemented as a simplified but real mechanism with real costs, spillage, a conserved and decaying soil-water store read by the existing growth code, and refusals with measured values, so the fallback was not needed.
